issues.legal_issue: An appellate court deciding whether to entertain a pure legal objection first raised after prolonged delay and abandoned before the lower appellate tribunal must consider the parties’ conduct and any resulting prejudice.
material_facts: In an eviction proceeding, the tenant initially denied the landlord-tenant relationship but did not plead that the notice terminating the tenancy was absent or invalid.
The tenant sought to add that technical objection by amendment about eight years after the eviction proceeding began.
The tenant did not press the notice objection before the appellate tribunal, which recorded that no other point had been urged.
Had the objection been raised earlier, the landlord could have withdrawn the eviction petition and brought a fresh one after serving the required notice; the delay caused prejudice to the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have permitted the tenant to argue the notice objection. Its judgment was set aside, and the eviction orders of the Rent Controller and Rent Control Tribunal were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Although a pure question of law not raised, or expressly abandoned, before the lower appellate court may sometimes be raised later, whether to permit it is a matter of judicial discretion. The court must consider all the circumstances, particularly the conduct of the party raising it and prejudice to the other party. The Court applied this principle in the context of an eviction appeal under Section 39(2) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, and referred to the amendment of the written statement under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. No earlier case was relied on for this principle.

rule.if: eviction_appeal and technical_notice_defense and defense_raised_after_long_delay and defense_abandoned_below and delay_prejudiced_landlord

predicates.eviction_appeal: A party appeals in an eviction proceeding.
predicates.technical_notice_defense: The tenant relies on a technical objection that a required notice terminating the tenancy was absent or invalid.
predicates.defense_raised_after_long_delay: The tenant raises the objection only after a prolonged period in the proceeding.
predicates.defense_abandoned_below: The tenant does not press the objection before the lower appellate tribunal.
predicates.delay_prejudiced_landlord: The delay prevents the landlord from pursuing a timely alternative course, such as withdrawing and refiling after giving notice.

issues.definition: When a tenant in an eviction appeal raises a technical notice objection only after prolonged delay, abandons it before the lower appellate tribunal, and the delay prejudices the landlord, the objection is not entertained.

issues.legal_issue: A ground listed in an appeal memorandum does not by itself establish that the point was argued before the lower appellate court when that court records that only other points were argued.
material_facts: The tenant’s appeal memorandum included grounds concerning the validity of the notice.
The lower appellate tribunal’s judgment stated that only specified points had been argued and that no other point was urged.
The tenant did not provide an affidavit from counsel asserting that the tribunal’s record of the arguments was mistaken or made under a misapprehension.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the tribunal’s account that the notice issue had not been argued; the grounds in the memorandum alone did not establish otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment recording that only specified points were argued is prima facie accepted as accurate. Listing a point in the memorandum of appeal is not enough to show that it was actually argued or pressed. A party alleging that the record is wrong may support that claim with a proper affidavit, preferably from counsel who argued the matter.

rule.if: appellate_proceeding and point_listed_in_appeal_memorandum and lower_court_records_only_other_points_urged and no_affidavit_supports_record_correction

predicates.appellate_proceeding: A court is reviewing a decision made in an appeal before a lower appellate tribunal.
predicates.point_listed_in_appeal_memorandum: A party includes the point among the grounds in its written appeal memorandum.
predicates.lower_court_records_only_other_points_ur: The lower appellate tribunal’s judgment states that only other specified points were argued.
predicates.no_affidavit_supports_record_correction: The party provides no affidavit, preferably from arguing counsel, stating that the tribunal’s account of the arguments was mistaken.

issues.definition: When a point is listed in an appeal memorandum but the tribunal records that only other points were argued, and no affidavit supports a claim that the record is mistaken, the point is not shown to have been argued.
